verifier_reason: test_outputs.py::test_seed_products_and_orders: The test failed in the call phase due to an assertion error

items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Names are mostly clear (openDangerConfirm, updateAfterSalePreview, currentAfterSaleOrderId). But the 3.5k-line file has very few comments, and the long inline delegation handlers rely on short names like `e`, `a` and `cb`.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: One 3573-line file. initEvents() wires every listener inline (pay/ship/cancel/aftersale/backup/reset/danger modal) and clearly runs well over 100 lines, which triggers the >100-line cap. UI handlers call shopTestAPI.* directly as their business layer.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: Inputs are validated (after-sale qty `Number.isInteger(val) || val < 0`, import errors). There is a silent `try { navigator.clipboard.writeText(...) } catch (_) {}`, though not on a mutation path. Hidden tests failed on seed products and out-of-stock rejection, so some edge cases are not covered.

items.name: Clerk workbench usability: amount breakdown, status hints, dangerous-action confirmation
items.name_zh: 店员工作台可用性：金额明细、状态提示与危险操作确认
items.evidence: openDangerConfirm is used for cancel (with the refund amount shown), restock and reset, and errors surface as toasts. Import overwrite runs `shopTestAPI.importData` without any confirmation, and after-sale submit has no explicit confirm beyond the modal preview.

items.name: Business logic lives in one place (UI and test API share it; integer-cent money)
items.name_zh: 业务逻辑集中且被界面与测试接口共用（金额按分计算）
items.evidence: The UI routes all operations through shopTestAPI (pay/ship/cancel/requestAfterSale/importData), so the logic is shared. Money uses float math with `round2(order.payable - order.refundedAmount)` and `.toFixed(2)` rather than integer cents.
